title: Output hygiene and tool-call reliability acceptance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines acceptance criteria and verification steps for consistent, debuggable structured output from streaming LLM responses and robust function/tool invocation behavior. The goal is to reduce customer operational burden when integrating function/tool calls over streamed outputs and to ensure deterministic error modes, resume semantics, and observability. This PRD clarifies expected envelopes, resume tokens, schema validation strategy, and retry/deduplication semantics for tool calls initiated by the model.
acceptance_criteria: Envelope format: Every streamed structured emission must be wrapped in a top-level JSON envelope with keys: "envelope_id", "seq", "type" and "payload". Types allowed: "fragment", "checkpoint", "tool_call", "tool_ack", "final".

Schema-first validation: The service must validate each checkpoint frame against the active schema version. Checkpoint frames invalid for structural errors must surface a clear error frame (type "final" with "error_class" and "human_message") and not be forwarded as a success to callers.

Progressive checkpoints: Streams must emit a checkpoint at most every N tokens (configurable; default 1024) and at logical boundaries (end of object/array). Checkpoints include a compact schema fingerprint and resume_token.

Resume semantics: Clients can reconnect and resume by supplying the last-seen resume_token. The resumed session must not re-execute side-effecting tool calls that previously completed successfully according to tool_ack frames tracked by the control plane.

Tool call handshake: For each proposed tool invocation the platform emits a tool_call frame with a call_id. The target service must respond with a tool_ack frame containing call_id and final_status in the same stream or via the control channel within 10s under normal load.

Idempotency and dedupe: call_id must be treated as an idempotency key. If a tool_ack arrives indicating an earlier completion, the runtime must not re-invoke the tool and must return the original result to the client.

Backpressure and queueing: If downstream tool endpoints are saturated, runtime must emit a warning checkpoint (type "checkpoint" with "backpressure" flag) and fall back to a configured policy: queue up to M pending calls or route to fallback model variant. Policy default: queue 5 then fallback to model-secondary.

Partial object repair: If stream ends with a truncated JSON payload (structural truncation), the platform must attempt a single deterministic repair pass using the last checkpoint and a best-effort filler strategy, emitting a repair_notice in the final frame. If repair fails, emit a final error frame with actionable diagnostics.

Observability events: Each tool_call lifecycle must emit tracer events: tool_call.requested, tool_call.sent, tool_call.ack, tool_call.completed, tool_call.failed. Events must include call_id, model_id, route_id, latency_ms and an error_class when applicable.

Error taxonomy: Define three classes surfaced to customers: recoverable_transient (retryable with backoff), permanent_business_error (do not retry), and policy_violation (block and escalate). Each final error frame must include one of these classes.
API compatibility: Existing non-streaming SDKs that request structured output must continue to receive identical envelope semantics in single-response mode (no ephemeral resume tokens required).
Load-tested SLOs: Under benchmarked medium load the median tool_call round-trip time reported to users must be <= 300ms and P95 <= 1.5s for in-region calls. SLO verification included in test_plan.

Deterministic replay for tests: Given fixed random seed and same model version, a stored sequence of client prompts plus tool_ack fixtures must produce identical envelope sequence in the deterministic test harness used by QA (modulo timestamps).
non_goals: This ticket does not redesign model-level function-calling semantics (prompt format or model markers) — focus is on platform-level envelopes and operational semantics.
We will not implement per-customer custom schema negotiation in this sprint; only server-side schema versions and migration paths are in scope.
No changes to pricing or billing semantics for tool invocations are part of this work.
design_decisions: Use lightweight envelope instead of inline ad-hoc JSON to enable clear stream boundaries and resumability.
Emit checkpoint frames periodically based on token count and syntactic boundaries to balance latency vs recoverability.
Control-plane tracking of tool_ack frames enables idempotency without requiring durable writes in the inference path; durable state written asynchronously with causal markers.
Expose resume_token to clients but treat it as opaque; server is authoritative for mapping resume_token -> checkpoint state.
open_questions: What is the default checkpoint frequency for short responses (<256 tokens)? Should we suppress checkpoints below 256 tokens to reduce noise?
Should the runtime attempt more than one repair pass for truncated payloads if the downstream shows intermittent connectivity failures?
Do we need a per-customer opt-out for resume semantics for strict regulatory customers who require full re-execution guarantees?
What telemetry retention window is required for forensic analysis of failed tool_call lifecycles?
dependencies: ENG-47211: stream framing infra and resume token plumbing
ENG-49821: control-plane tool-call eventing and durable call index
ENG-50100: SDK surface updates for envelope parsing and resume API
DES-141: client SDK UX for showing partial results and resume prompts
test_plan: Unit tests: envelope serializer/deserializer round-trip, invalid-envelope rejection, malformed-resume_token detection.
Integration: simulated tool endpoint that returns success/timeout/failure to validate backpressure behavior and fallback policy.
Chaos: drop network mid-stream and verify resume using resume_token produces stable final state (no double-invoke of tool).
Load test: run benchmark suite with 10k concurrent streaming sessions including 30% tool_call frequency; measure median and P95 tool_call latencies and checkpoint emission rate.
E2E regression: deterministic replay test with stored fixtures to ensure identical envelope sequence for given seed.
rollout_plan: Canary: roll to 10% of requests on hosted API with feature-flag that toggles envelope emission and resume tokens.
Observability gate: require zero increase in dropped tool_ack events and <2% increase in median token latency before progressing to 50%.
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over three days with rollback triggers for >5% increase in tool_call failures or any customer critical incident.
Documentation: publish SDK migration guide and best-practices for handling resume tokens and checkpoint frames prior to 50% rollout.
notes: PM/ENG sync 2025-02-25: agreed on envelope keys and checkpoint fingerprint format; ENG to deliver schema validator by 2025-03-01.
Design reviewed: Diego suggested including explicit "repair_notice" to surface attempted fixes for truncated fragments; landed in acceptance criteria.
Security: briefed security team about resume_token exposure; decided to treat tokens as bearer but short-lived (default 10m).
